title: "The Analysis Senior Responsible Officer"
description: "Business Critical work only. You take responsibility for the risks across the lifecycle and confirm the work is fit for its intended use."

{{< include /guidance/_partials/role-analysis-sro.qmd >}}

## When you are appointed

At scoping, as soon as the work is judged Business Critical, and before the analysis starts. The
register entry is made at the same time. If the work in front of you is not Business Critical, no
Analysis Senior Responsible Officer is appointed for it, and
[deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) is where that
judgement is made.

Being named afterwards does not work. What you are taking on is responsibility for risks across
the lifecycle, and most of the lifecycle will already have happened.

## Your part in each phase

| Phase | What is yours |
|---|---|
| [Phase 1. Engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) | Be named, and confirm the register entry is made |
| [Phase 2. Design](../02-design/index.qmd) | Confirm design governance has been followed |
| [Phase 3. Analysis](../03-analysis/index.qmd) | Stay aware of progress |
| [Phase 4. Delivery and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) | Approve the work as fit for its intended use, after the Lead Assurer has signed off |
| [Phase 5. Review](../05-review/index.qmd) | Revalidate the designation |

## What you are confirming, and what you are not

You confirm the work is **suitable for its intended use** before it is used. That is a judgement
about fitness for a purpose, made on the assurance evidence in front of you. It is not a second
technical review: the Lead Assurer has done that, and reports to you.

The designation is revalidated annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose, because reuse is
the change most likely to invalidate the assumptions the original was built on.

## You may also be the commissioner

The two roles can sit with the same person. Where they do, both sets of responsibilities apply,
and the independence the assurance level requires is unaffected: it governs the distance between
the assurer and the analyst, not between you and either of them.
